audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Capernaum house scene, roof opening, aphiemi release, Son of Humanity authority, Levi call, table fellowship, fasting/bridegroom, new cloth/wineskins, Sabbath grainfields, and Son of Humanity as lord of Sabbath.

verses.restored: When he entered Capernaum again after some days, it was heard that he was in the house.

familiar.text: And again he entered into Capernaum after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house.

modern.text: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home,

original.text: Καὶ ⸀εἰσελθὼν πάλιν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ διʼ ⸀ἡμερῶν ἠκούσθη ὅτι ⸂ἐν οἴκῳ⸃ ἐστίν·

verses.restored: Many gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even at the door; and he was speaking the word to them.

familiar.text: And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word unto them.

modern.text: they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.

original.text: ⸀καὶ συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον.

verses.restored: They came bringing to him a paralyzed man, carried by four.

familiar.text: And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four.

modern.text: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.

original.text: καὶ ἔρχονται ⸂φέροντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παραλυτικὸν⸃ αἰρόμενον ὑπὸ τεσσάρων.

verses.restored: Not being able to bring him because of the crowd, they removed the roof where he was; after digging through, they lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man lay.

familiar.text: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.

modern.text: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.

original.text: καὶ μὴ δυνάμενοι ⸀προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀπεστέγασαν τὴν στέγην ὅπου ἦν, καὶ ἐξορύξαντες χαλῶσι τὸν κράβαττον ⸀ὅπου ὁ παραλυτικὸς κατέκειτο.

verses.restored: Seeing their trust, Jesus said to the paralyzed man, Child, your sins/misalignments are released.

familiar.text: When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.

modern.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἰδὼν⸃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Τέκνον, ⸂ἀφίενταί σου⸃ αἱ ⸀ἁμαρτίαι.

verses.restored: Some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,

familiar.text: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

modern.text: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts,

original.text: ἦσαν δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐκεῖ καθήμενοι καὶ διαλογιζόμενοι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν·

verses.restored: Why does this one speak this way? He blasphemes. Who can release sins/misalignments except the Divine alone?

familiar.text: Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?

modern.text: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

original.text: Τί οὗτος οὕτως λαλεῖ; ⸀βλασφημεῖ· τίς δύναται ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός;

verses.restored: Immediately Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves, said to them, Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?

familiar.text: And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?

modern.text: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.

original.text: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐπιγνοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ ὅτι ⸀οὕτως διαλογίζονται ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ⸀λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ταῦτα διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;

verses.restored: Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, Your sins/misalignments are released, or to say, Rise, take your mat, and walk?

familiar.text: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

modern.text: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?

original.text: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· ⸀Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ ἆρον ⸂τὸν κράβαττόν σου⸃ καὶ περιπάτει;

verses.restored: But so that you may know that the Son of Humanity has authority on earth to release sins/misalignments, he said to the paralyzed man,

familiar.text: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,)

modern.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,

original.text: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ⸂ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας⸃— λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ·

verses.restored: I say to you: rise, take your mat, and go to your house.

familiar.text: I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

modern.text: “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

original.text: Σοὶ λέγω, ⸀ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.

verses.restored: He rose, immediately took the mat, and went out before all, so that all were amazed and glorified the Divine, saying, We never saw anything like this.

familiar.text: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.

modern.text: And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!” Jesus Calls Levi (Matthew 9:9–13; Luke 5:27–32)

original.text: καὶ ἠγέρθη ⸂καὶ εὐθὺς⸃ ἄρας τὸν κράβαττον ἐξῆλθεν ⸀ἔμπροσθεν πάντων, ὥστε ἐξίστασθαι πάντας καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν θεὸν λέγοντας ὅτι ⸂Οὕτως οὐδέποτε⸃ εἴδομεν.

verses.restored: He went out again beside the sea; all the crowd came to him, and he taught them.

familiar.text: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.

modern.text: Once again Jesus went out beside the sea. All the people came to Him, and He taught them there.

original.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Passing by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax office, and said to him, Follow me. He rose and followed him.

familiar.text: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

modern.text: As He was walking along, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Levi got up and followed Him.

original.text: καὶ παράγων εἶδεν Λευὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι. καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: As he reclined in his house, many tax collectors and sinners/misaligned ones were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at meat in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.

modern.text: While Jesus was dining at Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Him and His disciples—for there were many who followed Him.

original.text: Καὶ ⸀γίνεται κατακεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, ἦσαν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ⸀ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: The scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that he ate with sinners/misaligned ones and tax collectors, said to his disciples, Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?

familiar.text: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?

modern.text: When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people, they asked His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

original.text: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ⸂τῶν Φαρισαίων⸃ ⸀ἰδόντες ⸂ὅτι ἐσθίει⸃ μετὰ τῶν ⸂ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ τελωνῶν⸃ ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· ⸀Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν ⸂τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν⸃ ⸀ἐσθίει;

verses.restored: Hearing this, Jesus said to them, The strong do not need a physician, but those having harm. I did not come to call righteous ones, but sinners/misaligned ones.

familiar.text: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

modern.text: On hearing this, Jesus told them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” Questions about Fasting (Matthew 9:14–15; Luke 5:33–35)

original.text: καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς ⸀ὅτι Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλʼ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες· οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ⸀ἁμαρτωλούς.

verses.restored: John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to him, Why do John's disciples and the Pharisees' disciples fast, but your disciples do not fast?

familiar.text: And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?

modern.text: Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting. So people came to Jesus and asked, “Why don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees?”

original.text: Καὶ ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ ⸀Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύοντες. καὶ ἔρχονται καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν, οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν;

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

modern.text: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them? As long as He is with them, they cannot fast.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν νηστεύειν; ὅσον χρόνον ⸂ἔχουσιν τὸν νυμφίον μετʼ αὐτῶν⸃ οὐ δύνανται νηστεύειν·

verses.restored: Days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.

familiar.text: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

modern.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast. The Patches and the Wineskins (Matthew 9:16–17; Luke 5:36–39)

original.text: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ⸂ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ⸃.

verses.restored: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the new patch pulls away from the old, and a worse tear happens.

familiar.text: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.

modern.text: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. If he does, the new piece will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.

original.text: ⸀Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπιράπτει ἐπὶ ⸂ἱμάτιον παλαιόν⸃· εἰ δὲ μή, αἴρει τὸ πλήρωμα ⸀ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ τὸ καινὸν τοῦ παλαιοῦ, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.

verses.restored: No one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost, and so are the skins. But new wine is for fresh wineskins.

familiar.text: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.

modern.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.” The Lord of the Sabbath (1 Samuel 21:1–7; Matthew 12:1–8; Luke 6:1–5)

original.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή, ⸂ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος⸃ τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ⸂ἀπόλλυται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοί⸃. ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς ⸀καινούς.

verses.restored: It happened that he was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make their way, plucking heads of grain.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn.

modern.text: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain as they walked along.

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ⸂αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν παραπορεύεσθαι⸃ διὰ τῶν σπορίμων, καὶ ⸂οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο⸃ ὁδὸν ποιεῖν τίλλοντες τοὺς στάχυας.

verses.restored: The Pharisees said to him, Look, why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?

familiar.text: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?

modern.text: So the Pharisees said to Him, “Look, why are they doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

original.text: καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἴδε τί ⸀ποιοῦσιν τοῖς σάββασιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν;

verses.restored: He said to them, Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him,

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?

original.text: καὶ ⸀λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε χρείαν ἔσχεν καὶ ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: how he entered the house of the Divine in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those with him?

familiar.text: How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?

modern.text: During the high priesthood of Abiathar, he entered the house of God and ate the consecrated bread, which was lawful only for the priests. And he gave some to his companions as well.”

original.text: ⸀πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθὰρ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγεν, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ ⸂τοὺς ἱερεῖς⸃, καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ οὖσιν;

verses.restored: He said to them, The Sabbath came to be for the human, not the human for the Sabbath.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

modern.text: Then Jesus declared, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ σάββατον διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐγένετο ⸀καὶ οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τὸ σάββατον·

verses.restored: So the Son of Humanity is lord even of the Sabbath.

familiar.text: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

modern.text: Therefore, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

original.text: ὥστε κύριός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ τοῦ σαββάτου.
